speaker: Unknown
en: Can you all hear me?
zh: 大家都能听到我说话吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: All right.
zh: 好。

speaker: Unknown
en: Well, first, thanks for coming.
zh: 首先，感谢各位的到来。

speaker: Unknown
en: I can't believe there's anybody in the room, but that's very nice.
zh: 我不敢相信这个房间里还会有人，这真是太好了。

speaker: Unknown
en: My name is Jean Denis.
zh: 我叫 Jean Denis。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm CTO at a company called Town.
zh: 我是一家叫 Town 的公司的 CTO。

speaker: Unknown
en: We're not going to really talk about Town, so you can go to town.com and check that out if you want, but that's not the point of the talk today.
zh: 我们今天不会真的去聊 Town，所以如果你想了解的话可以去 town.com 看看，但那不是今天演讲的重点。

speaker: Unknown
en: I was CTO at Plaid for seven years, and then I was at Dropbox before.
zh: 我曾在 Plaid 做了七年 CTO，在那之前我在 Dropbox。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then, before that, I built software for hedge funds.
zh: 再往前，我为对冲基金开发软件。

speaker: Unknown
en: I've done lots of stuff in my career.
zh: 我的职业生涯做过很多事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: And right now, I'm working on assistance agents for normal people, not for engineers, but for basically everyone in America and the world.
zh: 现在我在做面向普通人的助理智能体，不是面向工程师，而是面向基本上全美国乃至全世界的每一个人。

speaker: Unknown
en: And one of the things we've been working on are systems where agents work with other agents, so agent to agent.
zh: 我们一直在做的事情之一，就是智能体与其他智能体协作的系统，也就是智能体对智能体。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the main idea is that we think there's huge network effects.
zh: 核心的想法是，我们认为这里面存在巨大的网络效应。

speaker: Unknown
en: If agents can work together to get things done for people, because in the real world, the way most of us do work is with other people, right?
zh: 如果智能体能够协同合作为人们把事情办成，因为在现实世界中，我们大多数人干活的方式就是与其他人一起干，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: More is better.
zh: 人越多越好。

speaker: Unknown
en: But actually, I don't think agent-to-agent makes much sense as a concept, so I want to reframe the entire talk in terms of search.
zh: 但实际上，我不认为智能体对智能体作为一个概念有多大意义，所以我想用搜索来重新构建整个演讲。

speaker: Unknown
en: Most LLM systems are just a search problem.
zh: 大多数 LLM 系统本质上就是一个搜索问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: And what you're trying to do is you're trying to make sure the context window, right before you either return results to the user or before a tool call, you're trying to make sure the context window has the right information for the user.
zh: 你要做的，是在你向用户返回结果之前、或者在发起一次工具调用之前，确保上下文窗口里装着对用户来说正确的信息。

speaker: Unknown
en: If you put the right information in the context window,
zh: 如果你把正确的信息放进上下文窗口，

speaker: Unknown
en: Then, based on the intelligence, so to speak, of the LLM, you will get the best result possible.
zh: 那么，基于 LLM 所谓的智能水平，你就会得到尽可能好的结果。

speaker: Unknown
en: So, you know, four years ago, the way we did that is humans would populate the context window manually.
zh: 所以，你知道，四年前，我们做这件事的方式是人类手动填充上下文窗口。

speaker: Unknown
en: Then a couple years ago, most people were ragging, so they were like, let's have a tool, like a search tool that can look across systems and bring the data in there.
zh: 然后几年之前，大多数人都在做 RAG，他们说，我们来做一个工具，比如一个搜索工具，可以跨系统检索并把数据带进来。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then people were like, well, that doesn't scale super well, it has issues.
zh: 然后人们又说，这个扩展性不太好，会有各种问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: And now we're all about agentic search, which is the idea that you give the agent a lot of tools, and it will search through the space of all content, and then hopefully before it makes a tool call, it has exactly the right content to make the right tool call to return the right information to the user.
zh: 现在我们都在讲智能体式搜索，也就是说你给智能体一大堆工具，它会在全部内容的空间里搜索，然后希望在它发起工具调用之前，它恰好拥有正确的内容，从而做出正确的工具调用，向用户返回正确的信息。

speaker: Unknown
en: And in this, by the way, there's no people.
zh: 顺便说一下，在这个过程中没有任何人。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's just one LLM call, like the one that matters, having the right context.
zh: 只是一次 LLM 调用，就是那一次真正重要的调用，要拥有正确的上下文。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's what you're trying to do.
zh: 这就是你要做的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: You're trying to engineer that system.
zh: 你要工程化地构建这个系统。

speaker: Unknown
en: Cool.
zh: 好。

speaker: Unknown
en: So what does that have to do with agent to agent?
zh: 那这跟智能体对智能体有什么关系呢？

speaker: Unknown
en: So I want you to imagine the following world.
zh: 我想让你们想象这样一个世界。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's not many agents that can do things.
zh: 并没有很多能干事情的智能体。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's just one agent, right?
zh: 只有一个智能体，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: And it has one context window.
zh: 它只有一个上下文窗口。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it has access to all the information in the universe.
zh: 而它可以访问宇宙中的所有信息。

speaker: Unknown
en: It can look at any one person's email.
zh: 它可以查看任何一个人的电子邮件。

speaker: Unknown
en: It can look at any company's information.
zh: 它可以查看任何一家公司的信息。

speaker: Unknown
en: It can look at any government's information.
zh: 它可以查看任何一个政府的信息。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it has it right there in the context window.
zh: 而且这些信息就摆放在它的上下文窗口里。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then you ask it to do something.
zh: 然后你让它去做某件事。

speaker: Unknown
en: You have your little system prompt before all that data.
zh: 在所有那些数据之前，你放上了你那段小小的系统提示词。

speaker: Unknown
en: And what's going to happen is it'll give you the best possible outcome.
zh: 接下来会发生的是，它会给你最好的可能结果。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that actually is a multi-Asian world.
zh: 而这实际上就是一个多智能体世界。（原文 multi-Asian 如此）

speaker: Unknown
en: It's just an agent that has access to all the world's information.
zh: 它只是一个可以访问全世界信息的智能体而已。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's the natural state of things.
zh: 这就是事物的自然状态。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's the ideal state of things.
zh: 这就是事物的理想状态。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's a problem with this state of things.
zh: 但这种状态存在一个问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the problem comes from cellular economics, something called the Coase theorem, and it says that basically even humans, if they all have access to all the right information and there's no transaction costs, we get the economically ideal outcome out of a contract or a negotiation.
zh: 这个问题来自细胞经济学（原文如此），一个叫做科斯定理的东西，它说的基本上是：即便是人类，如果他们都拥有所有正确的信息、并且不存在交易成本，我们从一份合同或一场谈判中就能得到经济上理想的结果。

speaker: Unknown
en: Well, it's the same thing.
zh: 这是一回事。

speaker: Unknown
en: We can't put all of the world's contacts.
zh: 我们没法把全世界所有的上下文都装进去。

speaker: Unknown
en: We can't make it available to the LLM.
zh: 我们不能把它开放给 LLM。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like theoretically even with infinite context window because of privacy and security.
zh: 比如理论上即使有无限的上下文窗口也不行，因为隐私和安全问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: We're humans, I don't let you look at my email, so there cannot be an agent that I'm willing to just let it look at my email all the time.
zh: 我们是人，我不会让你看我的邮箱，所以也不可能有一个智能体是我愿意让它一直看我的邮箱的。

speaker: Unknown
en: But if it existed, it would be very, very powerful.
zh: 但如果它存在，它将会非常、非常强大。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I think this is like, this is the test for a multi-agent system, which is how well does it approximate this?
zh: 所以我觉得这就是，这就是对一个多智能体系统的测试，也就是它对这个的逼近程度有多好。

speaker: Unknown
en: If it approximates this, that means if you can get the same data in your window that a perfect system that has access to all the world's data could, then you get the optimal outcome.
zh: 如果它逼近了这个，意思是如果你能在你的窗口里获得与一个能访问全世界所有数据的完美系统相同的数据，那么你就能得到最优的结果。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's what you need to try to do.
zh: 这就是你需要努力去做的事。

speaker: Unknown
en: So we're going to talk about five strategies that people use at various companies to try to get the right data into that LLM call with an externality.
zh: 所以我们要谈五个策略，是各家公司在不同情况下使用的，用来尝试把正确的数据带进那次 LLM 调用，同时带有一个外部性。

speaker: Unknown
en: So the first one is approximate access to everything within a trust boundary.
zh: 那么第一个是近似访问信任边界内的一切。

speaker: Unknown
en: So my wife and I, we have an agent together.
zh: 我和我太太，我们共用一个智能体。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that agent has access to my email and her email, including emails before we were married.
zh: 那个智能体可以访问我的邮箱和她的邮箱，包括我们结婚之前的邮件。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it's okay, she doesn't ask my agent questions about that, but she does ask about whether I scheduled something for our kids or if I followed up on some third-party thing.
zh: 这没关系，她不会向我的智能体问那些问题，但她确实会问我有没有为我们的孩子安排了什么事，或者我有没有跟进某个第三方的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so the fact that our agent has access to both of our systems is wonderful.
zh: 所以我们的智能体能访问我们两个人的系统这件事，非常棒。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the work context, this might be there's an HR team agent that has access to all the HR systems, just like an employee of the HR team would, or maybe as much access as the lowest employee in the HR team.
zh: 在工作场景下，这可能是一个 HR 团队智能体，它可以访问所有 HR 系统，就像 HR 团队的一名员工那样，或者权限和 HR 团队里最低级别的员工一样多。

speaker: Unknown
en: All the employees in the HR team have the ability to ask this agent questions, and boom, it gets pretty good results.
zh: HR 团队的所有员工都可以向这个智能体提问，然后砰，就能得到相当不错的结果。

speaker: Unknown
en: And this is very popular right now.
zh: 这个现在非常流行。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's very popular with IT teams and security teams because it's the same model as SAS for security, so it works really well.
zh: IT 团队和安全团队特别喜欢它，因为它和安全领域的 SAS 是同一个模式，所以效果非常好。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think it has a problem, which is a fundamental problem that if I wake up in the morning, it's like basically the only thing I think about, which is, does it get over time?
zh: 但我认为它有一个问题，一个根本性的问题，就是我早上醒来的时候，基本上我唯一在想的事情就是，它能不能随着时间推移？

speaker: Unknown
en: Does the system naturally require fewer humans?
zh: 这个系统会不会自然地需要更少的人？

speaker: Unknown
en: And then as the models get better, does this approach get better?
zh: 然后随着模型变好，这种方法会不会变得更好？

speaker: Unknown
en: And the problem with this approach is the answer is no to both.
zh: 这种方法的问题在于，两个问题的答案都是否。

speaker: Unknown
en: You still need humans to think about all the data, and you don't get magical de-siloification of your data.
zh: 你仍然需要人来思考所有的数据，而且你的数据不会神奇地被打破孤岛。

speaker: Unknown
en: You've just created a new silo because a human thought about it.
zh: 你只是创建了新的孤岛，因为有人思考过它。

speaker: Unknown
en: So the problem with this is I do think if this is your approach to building better AI, you're gonna be fucked in the next couple years.
zh: 所以问题在于，我真的认为如果这是你打造更好 AI 的方法，接下来几年你会完蛋的。

speaker: Unknown
en: But that's okay, you're fucked is my opportunity.
zh: 不过没关系，你完蛋就是我的机会。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm just not an asshole.
zh: 我只是不是个混蛋。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm sorry.
zh: 抱歉。

speaker: Unknown
en: That was mean.
zh: 那句话有点刻薄。

speaker: Unknown
en: But I think it's a good now way to think about it.
zh: 但我认为这是一个现在看待它的好方式。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's not the good endgame way to think about it.
zh: 但它不是终局的好的思考方式。

speaker: Unknown
en: The other approach, which I think is a little more clever, and I'm going to try to explain it, is basically you try to have tools that make a different tradeoff between power and privacy.
zh: 另一种方法，我觉得稍微更聪明一点，我来试着解释一下，基本上就是你尝试用工具在能力与隐私之间做一种不同的权衡。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I'm going to give you an example here.
zh: 我来给你举个例子。

speaker: Unknown
en: The use case is I want to ask my agent, is anyone in my company connected to someone on the finance team at Acme Corp?
zh: 这个用例是我想问我的智能体，我公司里有没有人和 Acme Corp 财务团队的某个人有联系？

speaker: Unknown
en: The no-silo way to do that is just give me access to everyone's Gmail in my company.
zh: 打破孤岛的做法就是直接让我访问我公司的所有人的 Gmail。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'll see who has emails with people from Acme Corp. Then I'll look at their profile on Google or LinkedIn.
zh: 我会看到谁和 Acme Corp 的人有邮件往来。然后我会看他们在 Google 或 LinkedIn 上的资料。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then I'll be like, oh, you seem to email a lot with the CFO.
zh: 然后我会说，哦，你好像经常和 CFO 发邮件。

speaker: Unknown
en: Can you do the intro for me?
zh: 你能帮我做个引荐吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: But obviously, silos, we don't want that.
zh: 但显然，孤岛，我们不想要那样。

speaker: Unknown
en: So what if you built a tool?
zh: 那如果你造一个工具呢？

speaker: Unknown
en: And what the tool did is it looked at everyone's Gmail.
zh: 这个工具做的事情是查看所有人的 Gmail。

speaker: Unknown
en: So that tool had access to everyone's Gmail.
zh: 所以这个工具可以访问所有人的 Gmail。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it just returned a relationship strength score.
zh: 而它只返回一个关系强度分数。

speaker: Unknown
en: So the tool, you would give it a domain, and you would say, I'm looking for someone who's a CFO.
zh: 你会给这个工具一个域名，然后说，我在找某个 CFO。

speaker: Unknown
en: It would look at everyone at the company who sent emails to that company, and then they would rank their score, and they would give you back the score.
zh: 它会查看公司里所有给那家公司发过邮件的人，然后给他们排名打分，然后把分数返回给你。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then the agent would get the score, and it would be cool.
zh: 然后智能体会拿到分数，这就很酷了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Then they would use the Slack tool to text that person to the company.
zh: 然后它会用 Slack 工具给公司里的那个人发消息。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's like, hey, Bob, I see that you're connected with Jane, who's the CFO at Acme Corp.
zh: 就像，嘿，Bob,我看到你和 Jane 有联系，她是 Acme Corp 的 CFO。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then Bob would be like, yes, I am.
zh: 然后 Bob 会说，是的，我认识她。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then your AI would be like, oh, can I draft an email, or can you draft an email introducing me?
zh: 然后你的 AI 会说，哦，我能起草一封邮件吗，或者你能起草一封介绍我的邮件吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: And then Bob would say yes, and he would do that, and you would be connected, and everything would be wonderful.
zh: 然后 Bob 会说可以，他会去做，然后你们就联系上了，一切都美好了。

speaker: Unknown
en: So this is actually a very cool approach.
zh: 所以这其实是一个非常酷的方法。

speaker: Unknown
en: I don't know how many of you do it.
zh: 我不知道在座有多少人这么做。

speaker: Unknown
en: We do this at town for a few things that we see a lot of our users do.
zh: 我们在 town 对一些我们看到很多用户都会做的事情采用这种方法。

speaker: Unknown
en: We ask ourselves, what is a privacy-preserving tool that all of our users would be okay existing?
zh: 我们问自己,什么样的隐私保护工具是我们所有用户都能接受存在的?

speaker: Unknown
en: They can opt out if they don't want it, but it has a natural network effect because it breaks through silos in an interesting way.
zh: 他们可以退出,如果他们不想要它,但它有一种天然的网络效应,因为它以一种有趣的方式打破了孤岛。

speaker: Unknown
en: Another one that's interesting here is letting other people put draft emails in your inbox.
zh: 另一个在这里有意思的做法是,让别人把草稿邮件放进你的收件箱。

speaker: Unknown
en: You let other people at your company draft emails on your behalf because they're going to ask you to anyway to get intros if they're on the sales team, so might as well save yourself a few clicks.
zh: 你让公司里的其他人在你名下起草邮件,因为如果他们在销售团队,他们反正都会请求你帮忙做介绍,那不如省掉自己几次点击。

speaker: Unknown
en: So the question here is, are people going to be okay with a privacy tradeoff that you make within a corporation?
zh: 所以这里的问题是,人们会不会接受你在公司内部做出的隐私权衡?

speaker: Unknown
en: Ah, bad, bad.
zh: 啊,糟糕,糟糕。

speaker: Unknown
en: Oh, boy.
zh: 哦,天哪。

speaker: Unknown
en: Within a corporation, that will, you know, mostly it works.
zh: 在公司内部,你知道,大多数情况下它是行得通的。

speaker: Unknown
en: So the problem here, again, is it's, again, manual and not dynamic.
zh: 所以这里的问题,还是那句话,它又是手动的,不是动态的。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's manual because humans need to think about the tools.
zh: 说它手动,是因为人类需要去思考这些工具。

speaker: Unknown
en: Maybe AI could build the tools.
zh: 也许 AI 可以构建这些工具。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it's also manual because you need to explain it to everyone that it's happening.
zh: 说它手动,还因为你需要向每个人解释这件事正在发生。

speaker: Unknown
en: Humans may not like it if this is happening, if they're not okay with the privacy security, the privacy kind of power trade-off that you've made.
zh: 如果这件事正在发生,如果他们对隐私安全、对隐私层面的权力权衡不满意,人类可能会不喜欢。

speaker: Unknown
en: Cool.
zh: 好。

speaker: Unknown
en: And again, this doesn't really get better as the AI gets better, which is a problem.
zh: 而且,这并不会随着 AI 变得更好而改善,这是一个问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: Cool, so now the third category, this one's super popular, but only mostly in the single user context.
zh: 好,现在是第三类,这一类超级流行,但主要只在单用户场景中。

speaker: Unknown
en: So this is, you know, like personal wikis in Clawland, that's what we would call it, but it's across teams.
zh: 这就是,你知道,比如 Clawland 里的个人 wiki,我们会这么叫它,但它是跨团队的。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's a shared silo.
zh: 它是一个共享的孤岛。

speaker: Unknown
en: Create a new place where data accumulates within your company, within subgroups of your company.
zh: 在你的公司内部、公司的子群体内部,创建一个新的数据积累的地方。

speaker: Unknown
en: And you start to put more and more stuff there over time.
zh: 然后随着时间的推移,你开始往那里放越来越多的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: And all the agents have access to that stuff because they have access to it.
zh: 而所有智能体都能访问那些东西,因为它们有访问权限。

speaker: Unknown
en: You no longer have information that would be okay to be shared that's stuck in a silo.
zh: 你不再有那些本来可以共享、却被困在孤岛里的信息。

speaker: Unknown
en: It now automatically filters out into this public space.
zh: 它现在会自动过滤流入这个公共空间。

speaker: Unknown
en: Examples, shared skills.
zh: 例子,共享技能。

speaker: Unknown
en: If you code in an organization, probably in your repo you have shared skills.
zh: 如果你在一个组织里写代码,很可能在你的代码仓库里有共享技能。

speaker: Unknown
en: Anyone can make them better.
zh: 任何人都可以把它们做得更好。

speaker: Unknown
en: Someone has a better way to profile your database or whatever.
zh: 某人对你的数据库有更好的性能分析方法,或者别的什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: They can write the skill.
zh: 他们可以写这个技能。

speaker: Unknown
en: Next time someone's sitting there is like, oh my god, the database query's slow.
zh: 下次有人坐在那里,心想,天哪,数据库查询太慢了。

speaker: Unknown
en: It uses the profiling skill and everyone's a better engineer.
zh: 它就会使用这个性能分析技能,然后每个人都成了更好的工程师。

speaker: Unknown
en: So that's one version.
zh: 这是一种版本。

speaker: Unknown
en: The other one that's pretty popular is people decide they have some shared mediums like a wiki, Airtable, et cetera, and they have a skill that says, hey, put more data in there over time.
zh: 另一个很流行的做法是,人们决定拥有一些共享媒介,比如 wiki、Airtable 等等,然后他们有一个技能,说,嘿,随着时间推移往里面放更多数据。

speaker: Unknown
en: So these are cool, and they work as long as your agents have those tools and also some trajectory incentives to really get data out in and out of these shared silos.
zh: 这些都很酷,而且只要你的智能体拥有那些工具,并且有一些轨迹激励,真正把数据从这些共享孤岛中放进去取出来,它们就能工作。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think the next version of this that a few people are working on is you have a sweeper AI.
zh: 我认为下一个版本,有几个人正在做的,是你有一个清扫 AI。

speaker: Unknown
en: So this is actually, if there's one good idea in this talk,
zh: 所以这其实是,如果这个演讲里有一个好想法,

speaker: Unknown
en: that I think works really well is this.
zh: 我认为效果非常好的就是它。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's a sweeper AI.
zh: 它是一个清扫 AI。

speaker: Unknown
en: So you have an AI inside each private silo.
zh: 所以你在每个私人孤岛里都有一个 AI。

speaker: Unknown
en: An AI has a policy about what has to stay in the silo.
zh: 这个 AI 有一套关于什么必须留在孤岛内的策略。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then it also has a description of all the shared spaces that you have.
zh: 然后它还有一份对所有你拥有的共享空间的描述。

speaker: Unknown
en: And at the end of the day, it looks at new information in a silo, and it puts it in the public spaces.
zh: 在一天结束时,它会查看孤岛里的新信息,并把它放进公共空间。

speaker: Unknown
en: Well, public, public to your company.
zh: 好吧,公共,是对你的公司公共。

speaker: Unknown
en: So this is the same as the personal wiki that you all have AI building for you at the end of the day so that it knows your goals and your friends and all that stuff, but it's at the company level.
zh: 这和你们每个人都有 AI 在一天结束时为你构建的个人 wiki 是一样的,这样它了解你的目标、你的朋友等等,只不过这是在公司层面。

speaker: Unknown
en: The hard part is how do we pick what private information is okay to share and to put it in shared silos?
zh: 困难的部分是,我们如何决定哪些私人信息可以共享、放进共享孤岛?

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think there's two approaches.
zh: 我认为有两种方法。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's the ask-a-human approach.
zh: 一种是询问人类的方法。

speaker: Unknown
en: So this is like the LLM comes up with a list of things to contribute, and then it asks the user, hey, are you okay with me putting this in their shared space?
zh: 就是 LLM 想出一份要贡献的内容清单,然后询问用户,嘿,你介意我把这个放进他们的共享空间吗?

speaker: Unknown
en: And you read it.
zh: 然后你读了一遍。

speaker: Unknown
en: You're like, yeah, saved you a bunch of time, right?
zh: 你心想，是啊，帮你省了不少时间，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, you weren't going to do it otherwise.
zh: 我是说，不然你本来也不会去做这件事。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think the other version is you actually ask the LLM to enforce a policy.
zh: 我认为另一种版本是你真的让 LLM 来执行一项政策。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think that actually is where things are going to go very, very quickly.
zh: 而我认为事情实际上很快、很快就会朝这个方向发展。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think in the next six months we'll have a bunch of systems where companies have trusted an LLM with a policy to automatically surface more and more information that otherwise would have been private into a public space.
zh: 我认为在未来六个月内，我们会看到一堆这样的系统：公司把一项政策托付给 LLM,让它自动把越来越多的、原本属于私密的信息披露到公开空间里。

speaker: Unknown
en: If you're like at a Fortune 500 enterprise company, unfortunately,
zh: 如果你在一家财富 500 强企业公司，很遗憾，

speaker: Unknown
en: I don't think that's going to happen for a while, but I think if you look at smaller companies, like 10, 50% employees, high trust, like low likelihood of one doing bad with the data, where it's really clear to know what data couldn't be shared, basically finance and HR data, you're going to see a ton of this.
zh: 我觉得这短期内不会发生，但如果你看那些更小的公司，比如 10 个、50% 员工的规模，高信任度，有人滥用数据的可能性很低，而且很清楚哪些数据不能共享——基本上就是财务和 HR 数据——你会看到大量这种做法。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the cool thing here is this really improves trajectories of systems on common work.
zh: 而这里很酷的一点是，这真的能改善系统在常见工作上的表现轨迹。

speaker: Unknown
en: That was third approach.
zh: 那是第三种方法。

speaker: Unknown
en: Fourth approach is pretty obvious.
zh: 第四种方法很显而易见。

speaker: Unknown
en: Use humans as the conduit for information.
zh: 用人作为信息的管道。

speaker: Unknown
en: So this is like traditional agent to agent.
zh: 这就是传统的智能体对智能体。

speaker: Unknown
en: My agent asks your agent, hey, who is connected to someone of the finance team at Acme Corp?
zh: 我的智能体问你的智能体，嘿，谁和 Acme Corp 财务团队的某个人有联系？

speaker: Unknown
en: You as a human see the request and you're like, yeah, I'm okay with that.
zh: 你作为人类看到这个请求，然后心想，嗯，我可以接受。

speaker: Unknown
en: Go and find the information inside of my email.
zh: 去在我的邮件里找这个信息吧。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then it shows you the result.
zh: 然后它把结果展示给你。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then you're like, yes, I'm okay with that result.
zh: 然后你说，好，我对这个结果没问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: Going to the person who asked.
zh: 去发给提出请求的那个人。

speaker: Unknown
en: The big problem with it is for any request that has low, where it's like only a few people will have the information, you're kind of spamming everyone the request.
zh: 它的大问题在于，对于那些只有少数人才掌握信息的请求，你基本上是在把请求群发给所有人。

speaker: Unknown
en: So if I ask this question, 100 person company, 100 people are being pinged on Slack, being approved on these requests to farm your personal network for the answer to this question.
zh: 所以如果我问这个问题，在一家 100 人的公司里，100 个人都会在 Slack 上被 ping 到，被请求批准——为了这个问题的答案去开发你的个人人脉。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's not very efficient.
zh: 这不是很高效。

speaker: Unknown
en: So that's why there's a better version of it, which this is very powerful, but I haven't seen it in practice much.
zh: 所以才有一个更好的版本，这个方法非常强大，但我在实践中还没怎么见到。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's a black box approach.
zh: 那就是黑箱方法。

speaker: Unknown
en: I wish I had a diagram for this.
zh: 我真希望能有一张示意图来讲这个。

speaker: Unknown
en: Unfortunately for you all, I do not.
zh: 很不幸，各位，我没有。

speaker: Unknown
en: So here's what this means.
zh: 那么它的意思是这样的。

speaker: Unknown
en: The black box approach is where when you ask a question that can only be answered by looking at information in other people's silos, you have an LLM, the trace of which no one has access to,
zh: 黑箱方法是指，当你提出一个只能通过查看别人信息孤岛里的数据才能回答的问题时，你有一个 LLM,它的执行轨迹没有人能访问，

speaker: Unknown
en: That gets access to all the data and it gets to the answer, right?
zh: 它能访问所有数据，并且它找到了答案，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: Like I say get to the answer, it either gets the answer or it's about to do any tool call that's a right.
zh: 我说找到答案，是指它要么得到了答案，要么即将执行任何这样的工具调用。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then it looks at what information did it need to make that tool call and it only asks the people who own that information for their approval to do the tool call.
zh: 然后它回看执行这个工具调用需要哪些信息，并且只向拥有那些信息的人请求批准执行该工具调用。

speaker: Unknown
en: So in the example before that I gave, when I asked 100 people at my company, hey, do you know the CFO at Acme Corp?
zh: 所以在我之前给的那个例子里，当我问我公司的 100 个人，嘿，你认识 Acme Corp 的 CFO 吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: The request goes to everyone's agents in my company.
zh: 这个请求会发到我公司每个人的智能体那里。

speaker: Unknown
en: All of their agents look in their Gmail and their private silos to see if they're connected to the CFO.
zh: 他们所有的智能体会在他们的 Gmail 和各自的私有信息孤岛里查看他们是否和这位 CFO 有联系。

speaker: Unknown
en: That happens automatically.
zh: 这一步是自动完成的。

speaker: Unknown
en: No human is being asked for approval for that to happen.
zh: 没有任何人被请求为此批准。

speaker: Unknown
en: Then the agent in the black box gets the list of the 20 people who are connected.
zh: 然后黑箱里的智能体拿到那 20 个有联系的人的名单。

speaker: Unknown
en: It looks at context from the emails to determine who has the strongest connection.
zh: 它查看邮件中的上下文来确定谁有最强的联系。

speaker: Unknown
en: It determines that it's Bob.
zh: 它确定是 Bob。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then it just asks Bob, hey, Jean Denis wants you to introduce him to Jane, the CFO at Acme Corp.
zh: 然后它只问 Bob:嘿,Jean Denis 想让你把他介绍给 Acme Corp 的 CFO Jane。

speaker: Unknown
en: I know you're well-connected to her.
zh: 我知道你和她的关系很紧密。

speaker: Unknown
en: Am I okay sharing that bit of information with Jean Denis?
zh: 我可以把这一点信息分享给 Jean Denis 吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: And you're like, yeah, sure.
zh: 然后你说，嗯，当然。

speaker: Unknown
en: You click yes.
zh: 你点了同意。

speaker: Unknown
en: No big deal.
zh: 没什么大不了的。

speaker: Unknown
en: The important thing is you have to trust the black box.
zh: 关键在于你必须信任这个黑箱。

speaker: Unknown
en: So you have to trust that you can break down all the silos for an LLM that has full access and that doesn't ask for permission until there's this sharing moment or this right step.
zh: 所以你必须相信，你可以把所有的信息孤岛都打通给一个拥有完全访问权限的 LLM,而它直到出现这个分享时刻或这类步骤之前都不会请求许可。

speaker: Unknown
en: So actually, within a company, this is not impossible to do, and actually your security and compliance team can get okay with it.
zh: 所以实际上，在公司内部，这并非不可能做到，而且你的安全和合规团队是可以接受它的。

speaker: Unknown
en: You just have to have, you have to be sure that the human in the loop step is correct, and you have to be sure that you're not letting other information go through with the last answer.
zh: 你只需要确保，人工介入的环节是正确的，而且你要确保没有让其他信息随着最后那个答案一起泄漏出去。

speaker: Unknown
en: So, you know, like, the nightmare scenarios and things like this are things like, sorry, I'm like,
zh: 所以，你知道，比如说，最糟糕的情形和类似的事情是这样的，抱歉，我有点，

speaker: Unknown
en: We have plenty of time.
zh: 我们时间很充裕。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm almost done, so it's great.
zh: 我快讲完了，所以很好。

speaker: Unknown
en: The nightmare scenarios with things like this is someone asks a question like, are you connected to a recruiter at the other company that you have no business being recruited to as a way for them to find out that you're interviewing somewhere else, right?
zh: 这种事情的噩梦场景是，有人问一个问题，比如，你是不是和另一家公司的招聘人员有联系，而你根本不该被那家公司招募，以此作为一种方式让他们发现你正在别处面试，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: So you can still sometimes with the black box inadvertently get information out that you shouldn't be able to.
zh: 所以即使是在黑箱里，你有时仍然会不经意地泄露本不该能泄露出去的信息。

speaker: Unknown
en: You have to really think about how you build a great system.
zh: 你必须认真思考如何构建一个优秀的系统。

speaker: Unknown
en: So those are the approaches.
zh: 以上就是这些方法。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think if I were to bet on one that has immediate ROI that we're going to all see in both open source claw-ish worlds and in small companies, it's going to be the wiki that's automatically created by AI, the information base that's kept up to date.
zh: 我想，如果要我押注一个能带来即时 ROI、并且我们在开源的 claw 类世界和小公司里都会看到的方向，那就是由 AI 自动创建的 wiki，也就是保持更新的信息库。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think there will be database versions of it, wiki versions of it, and I think more and more we're going to trust LLMs to make the decision about what's okay to share and what's not.
zh: 我想会有数据库版本、wiki 版本，而且我们会越来越信任 LLM 来决定什么可以分享、什么不可以。

speaker: Unknown
en: There are problems, so prompted junction in the silos can be a real problem, obviously.
zh: 当然也存在问题，比如信息孤岛中的提示词注入可能是个真实的问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: So if you have a silo that has like, that's more open and someone can put something bad in there and then that, as part of the energetic search, you pull it out, you know, bad things can happen.
zh: 如果你有一个比较开放的信息孤岛，有人可以在里面放入恶意内容，然后作为主动式检索的一部分，你把它检索出来，你知道，坏事就可能发生。

speaker: Unknown
en: You can have, it's very easy to have a shared wiki that just goes like totally off the rails.
zh: 你可能会遇到，共享 wiki 很容易就完全脱轨。

speaker: Unknown
en: You know, like the information there, one piece of information there is incorrect because Llama made a mistake and then it like poisons it forever.
zh: 你知道，比如那里的信息中，有一条信息因为 Llama 犯了个错误而不正确，然后就永远地污染了整个库。

speaker: Unknown
en: I have a personal wiki that thinks my agent's name is Apex right now but I renamed my agent a month ago to Ivy and like somewhere in memory bank of my like setup Apex lives and so I can't get rid of it.
zh: 我有一个个人 wiki，它现在认为我的智能体叫 Apex，但我一个月前就把我的智能体改名为 Ivy 了，而且在我某个设置的记忆库深处 Apex 仍然存在，所以我没法摆脱它。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's fine for Apex, that's a funny one but it's like much more difficult if it's a really wrong piece of information about your business.
zh: 对 Apex 来说这没什么，这是个有趣的例子，但如果是一条关于你业务的严重错误的信息，那就要难办得多。

speaker: Unknown
en: If you don't have human in the loop for any of the steps, obviously, there'll be false positives and wrong disclosures.
zh: 如果任何步骤都没有人工参与，显然会出现误报和错误的披露。

speaker: Unknown
en: You know, sometimes when there's a wrong disclosure of information, someone gets fired.
zh: 你知道，有时候当出现错误的信息披露，会有人被解雇。

speaker: Unknown
en: Someone, there's a wrong disclosure, it doesn't matter at all.
zh: 有时候出现错误披露，却完全无所谓。

speaker: Unknown
en: Sometimes a customer sues you.
zh: 有时候客户会起诉你。

speaker: Unknown
en: So, you know, you gotta be careful.
zh: 所以，你知道，你必须小心。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then, I think...
zh: 然后，我想……

speaker: Unknown
en: This all sounds nice, but who approves what, what's logged, what's reversible?
zh: 这些听起来都不错，但谁来批准什么、记录什么日志、什么是可回滚的？

speaker: Unknown
en: The black box idea is really great, but it can't truly be a black box.
zh: 黑箱的想法真的很棒，但它不能真正成为一个黑箱。

speaker: Unknown
en: Someone at your company will want to audit it at some point.
zh: 你的公司里总有人会在某个时候想要审计它。

speaker: Unknown
en: They want to understand what's going in there, right?
zh: 他们想了解里面发生了什么，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: So at some level, there must be some person in the CISO suite or somewhere that has access to all the data.
zh: 所以在某种程度上，必须有一个在 CISO 团队或其他什么地方的人，能访问所有数据。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: What do I think?
zh: 我怎么看？

speaker: Unknown
en: Well, I do think the frontier is auto, so I've said that.
zh: 嗯，我确实认为前沿是 auto，这一点我说过了。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think in coding, we used to approve everything.
zh: 我想在编程领域，我们过去要批准每一件事。

speaker: Unknown
en: Then we were like, YOLO, live dangerously.
zh: 然后我们说，YOLO，活得冒险一点。

speaker: Unknown
en: And now the gods at Anthropic have granted us auto mode.
zh: 现在 Anthropic 的众神赐予了我们 auto 模式。

speaker: Unknown
en: And auto mode tries to figure out when we're maybe being a little silly, and it tells us, well, I think A to A across information silos will be the same way.
zh: auto 模式会试图判断我们什么时候可能有点犯傻，它会告诉我们，嗯，我认为跨信息孤岛的 A to A 也会是同样的方式。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think what's going to happen is we're going to get comfortable with low sensitivity information being pulled out and put into common spaces.
zh: 我想会发生的事情是，我们会逐渐适应低敏感度的信息被提取出来放进公共空间。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then we will have a place that's like human review or always human approved.
zh: 然后我们会设立一个需要人工审核或始终需要人工批准的地方。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then over time, what's going to happen is the LLMs will get more powerful.
zh: 随着时间推移，会发生的事情是 LLM 会变得更强大。

speaker: Unknown
en: We will be better at encoding safe policies within them.
zh: 我们会更擅长在其中编码安全策略。

speaker: Unknown
en: We will be better at designing for the really hard areas, tools that get the privacy tradeoff correct.
zh: 我们会更擅长针对真正困难的领域设计工具，把隐私权衡做对。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it'll just be more and more auto for building shared silos and even sometimes for deciding whether it involve a human.
zh: 而且构建共享信息孤岛、甚至有时决定是否需要人工参与，都会变得越来越 auto。

speaker: Unknown
en: So the example that I have is like if I ask for notes from a weekly recurring call with
zh: 举个例子，比如我想要我们与

speaker: Unknown
en: You know, a supplier of ours and their finance team, maybe the LM's like, oh, well, given your role, I don't need to ask anyone on those teams for permission, I can just share the notes with you.
zh: 你知道，我们的某个供应商及其财务团队的每周例行通话的会议记录，也许 LLM 会说，哦，好吧，鉴于你的角色，我不需要向那些团队的任何人请求许可，我可以直接把记录分享给你。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's like, it's fine.
zh: 这就像，没问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: They can look at the content, they can see what my role is, they can decide from a risk perspective, I'm okay with that disclosure.
zh: 它可以查看内容，可以看到我的角色是什么，可以从风险的角度决定，我对这次披露没有意见。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the cool thing about auto, by the way, is if you design your systems that way, it'll scale with model capacity.
zh: 顺便说一句，auto 的妙处在于，如果你按这种方式设计你的系统，它会随模型能力一起扩展。

speaker: Unknown
en: So my encouragement would be, like, you need to start, if you have agent-to-agent or work across silos, which I think is a better way to think about it, definitely define a low-sensitivity zone where you're okay with the LLM making a call.
zh: 所以我的建议是，你需要开始，如果你有智能体到智能体或跨信息孤岛的工作——我认为这是更好的思考方式——一定要定义一个低敏感度区域，在这个区域内你可以接受 LLM 做判断。

speaker: Unknown
en: And get okay with that, and then magically, as time goes on, it'll get bigger, and your system will naturally get more powerful, which is what you want, because you want to be on a beach.
zh: 接受这一点，然后神奇的是，随着时间推移，这个区域会变大，你的系统自然会更强大，这正是你想要的，因为你想要在海滩上。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's what you want to do.
zh: 那才是你想做的事。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's what I want to be.
zh: 那就是我想做的。

speaker: Unknown
en: My kids in Hawaii.
zh: 在夏威夷和我的孩子们在一起。

speaker: Unknown
en: Okay, network effects.
zh: 好的，网络效应。

speaker: Unknown
en: I have one minute.
zh: 我还有一分钟。

speaker: Unknown
en: This is the conclusion.
zh: 这是结论部分。

speaker: Unknown
en: So we talked about five approaches, blah, blah, blah, trust boundaries, custom tools, shared silos, humans in the loop, and this human in the loop black box version.
zh: 所以我们谈了五种方法，等等等等，信任边界、自定义工具、共享筒仓、人在回路，还有这个人在回路的黑箱版本。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think this stuff is very powerful.
zh: 我认为这些东西非常强大。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think the interesting questions a little bit are,
zh: 我认为有点意思的问题在于，

speaker: Unknown
en: Within companies, I think this will all work very soon.
zh: 在公司内部，我认为这一切很快就会实现。

speaker: Unknown
en: The big question is, how comfortable are we with something like an auto mode around privacy?
zh: 最大的问题是，我们对隐私方面的某种自动模式有多放心？

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think the really interesting question that I don't have an answer for, but I think whoever does this will be wealthier than I am, is if you can think of...
zh: 而我认为真正有意思的问题——我没有答案，但我认为谁能做到这一点就会比我更富有——是如果你能想到……

speaker: Unknown
en: Scenarios where you can get multiple companies to agree to their information silos, having a common agent working across them.
zh: 这样的场景：让多家公司同意把他们的信息筒仓交给一个共同的智能体在其间工作。

speaker: Unknown
en: So there's like a company that I will name somewhere in the world working on like finance stuff where they have a lot of investment banks.
zh: 所以世界上有一家我不点名提到了的公司，在做金融相关的事情，他们有很多投资银行。

speaker: Unknown
en: And actually the investment banks, there's a benefit to them sharing private data about private companies for purposes of things like lending.
zh: 而实际上，这些投资银行在共享关于私营公司的私密数据方面，对贷款之类的事情是有好处的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And they're starting to look in this direction where they're trusting each other's agents to be able to work across what before would have been private information with agents deciding what can be accessed and not.
zh: 而他们开始朝这个方向看，即信任彼此的智能体，能够在以前属于私密信息的数据之间开展工作，由智能体决定什么可以访问、什么不可以。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it's cool.
zh: 这很酷。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's very cool.
zh: 非常酷。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think once you find some use cases across companies, I think that would be a really good beachhead to move more in this direction.
zh: 而且我认为，一旦你找到一些跨公司的用例，我认为那会是一个很好的滩头阵地，可以进一步朝这个方向推进。

speaker: Unknown
en: So, yeah.
zh: 所以，是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: You know, as a human, though, I ask myself, do I trust a future where agents make all the decisions around privacy?
zh: 不过，你知道，作为一个人类，我问自己，我是否信任一个由智能体做出所有隐私决定的未来？

speaker: Unknown
en: I don't know about that.
zh: 这个我说不好。

speaker: Unknown
en: I just think it is, for better or worse, the direction things are going.
zh: 我只是觉得，无论好坏，事情正朝这个方向发展。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I'm, like, so good on time.
zh: 而且，我时间上刚好差不多。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I'm on time.
zh: 所以我是准时的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Thank you for coming.
zh: 谢谢大家前来。

speaker: Unknown
en: Again, yeah.
zh: 再次，是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Thanks for being here.
zh: 感谢各位到场。

speaker: Unknown
en: Thank you.
zh: 谢谢。
